question.leadin: Following the failure of the Shimabara Rebellion during this period, Christians were forced underground.
question.text: Name this last shogunate [show-gun-ate] of Japan. Commodore Matthew Perry entered Japan while this shogunate was in power.
question.clue: Because of the Shimbara rebellion, this period's government increased its proscription of Christians.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
swap.text: During the Edo period, Japan was ruled by this family, for whom the period is also sometimes named. Ieyasu (EE-ay-ah-soo), a member of this family, won the Battle of Sekigahara to begin the Edo period.
swap.clue: This Japanese clan the ruled from Edo. This clan headed the last feudal military government of Japan, and their first shogun was Ieyasu.

question.leadin: Give the following about earthquakes that have devastated Japan.
question.text: Both the 2011 and 1923 earthquakes were centered near this largest Japanese island.
question.clue: By far the largest of the four main islands is this one, home to Tokyo, Kyoto, and Nagoya.

swap.leadin: Give the following about surprise attacks in Japanese history.
swap.text: In the 1560 Battle of Okehazama, this daimyo's forces sneaked to the rear of the opposing army, killing the opposing leader at his tent. This unifier of Japan was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.
swap.clue: This man's troops used matchlocks to repulse the charge of Takeda cavalry at the Battle of Nagashino.

question.leadin: Rudolf von Gneist helped create a new constitution during this period.
question.text: Name this period in Japanese history following the end of the Tokugawa Shogunate. This period is named for an emperor whose reign saw a resurgence of imperial power.
question.clue: Near the beginning of this period, the Battle of Hakodate caused the dissolution of the Republic of Ezo at the end of the Boshin War.

swap.leadin: This man led successful campaigns at Inabayama Castle and Anegawa despite his past as a lowly sandal-bearer.
swap.text: Name this man, the successor of Oda Nobunaga, who later crucified twenty-six Christians in Nagasaki and restricted the carrying of weapons to the samurai class.
swap.clue: This leader, who initiated construction of Osaka Castle, led failed invasions of Korea in 1592 and 1598.

question.leadin: This event's instigator took advantage of his favored status within the imperial court to march his troops through Kyoto without raising suspicions.
question.text: Name this event in which a Japanese warlord committed seppuku after being ambushed during a tea ceremony. Its instigator, Akechi Mitsuhide, was later defeated at the Battle of Yamazaki by the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
question.answerHtml: Honno-ji incident [accept, but DO NOT REVEAL suicide of Oda Nobunaga or betrayal of Oda Nobunaga or the coup against Oda Nobunaga or equivalents]
question.clue: This coup that ended in Oda Nobunaga's forced suicide. It occurred at a Kyoto temple and was orchestrated by Akechi Mitsuhide.

swap.text: Although the shogunate was centered on Kamakura, the official capital and residence of the emperor remained this western city, whose name simply means "capital city."
swap.clue: Companies with headquarters in this city include Nichicon, Murata, and Ninetendo.

question.text: Yoshitsune's victories over the Taira clan enabled Minamoto Yoritomo to begin the Kamakura period by becoming the first man to claim this title, the military ruler of Japan.
question.clue: Ishida Mitsunari was defeated by a prominent holder of this title at the Battle of Sekigahara.

swap.leadin: Of the hundreds of exploding balloons sent by this group to the U.S., only one managed to cause any damage, landing in Oregon and killing several schoolchildren who checked it out.
swap.text: Name this group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.
swap.answerHtml: Unit 731 [or Nana-san-ichi Butai, or Manchu Detachment 731, or 731 Regiment, or Ishii Unit]
swap.clue: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.

question.text: This city near the Kyoto-Kobe-Osaka metropolis contains lots of tame deer that roam around its many temples. Todai-ji, 7 other temples, and a forest make up the UNESCO World Heritage site of this city.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.text: After Japan's defeat in World War II, Hirohito managed to avoid the war crimes trials that condemned this Prime Minister. This man survived a 1945 suicide attempt before his execution by hanging in 1946.
swap.clue: This leader of the Chahar Expeditionary Force ordered troops to attack Hebei Province following the Marco Polo incident.

question.text: In correspondence with Emperor Yang of Sui, this prince encouraged him to call Japan by Nihon. Through the Seventeen-Article Constitution, he promoted Buddhism as Japan's state religion.

swap.text: The post-World War II Japanese constitution contained this article, which renounced the national right to war and use of force in international disputes. Despite this article, Japan maintains self-defense forces that serve as a de facto military.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Russo-Japanese conflict FTPE.
question.text: This battle fought in 1939 was a response to an incursion of Mongolian cavalry into the territory of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo and resulted in a Russian victory that may have encouraged Japan to fight against the U.S. rather than Russia in the Pacific.
question.answerHtml: the Battle of Khalkin Gol (or the Battle of Khalkhin Lake or the Nomonhan Incident)
question.clue: This August 1939 clash on the Manchurian-Mongolian frontier resulted in a clear victory for Soviet armor commanded by the then-unknown General Zhukov over the Kwantung Army. Partly as a result, Stalin would be free to transfer Siberian forces to Europe following Operation Barbarossa.

swap.leadin: Four brothers from this family established its "four houses"-the Northern, Southern, Ceremonial, and Capital-only to all die in the same year from smallpox.
swap.text: Name this family that established a semi-hereditary claim on the positions of sessho and kampaku after the 8th century, allowing their patriarchs to exercise imperial authority by marrying their daughters to the emperor.
swap.clue: This clan gained much power in the Heian period by marrying its daughters into the imperial family. Michinaga of this clan was the father-in-law of four emperors and grandfather to three.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the rise of a Japanese family.
question.text: This family, most notably led by Yoritomo, rebelled against the Taira clan in 1180. Their victory led to the establishment of the first bakufu, or shogunate, and the start of the Kamakura period.
question.clue: They were defeated by their main rivals in the Heiji Rebellion, after which many of them were mercifully sent into exile including Noriyori, the younger brother of the main members.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Genpei War.
swap.text: The war concluded with this naval battle won by Yoshitsune off Honshu's southern coast, in Shimonoseki Strait. After it, Yoshitsune's older brother, Minamoto Yuritomo, established the Kamakura shogunate.
swap.clue: This battle saw Taguchi Shigeyoshi reveal the location of the Emperor's ship, and both the child-emperor Antoku and his grandmother, the widow of Kiyomori, committed suicide.

question.text: The foremost predecessor of the LDP was the Liberal Party, which was led by this towering figure of post-WWII Japanese politics. He served as Prime Minister five times between 1946 and 1954, and formulated a namesake Doctrine for Japan's postwar recovery.

swap.text: The story is often backdated to apply to the rule of this man, who became the first shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate after he'd originally allied with Go-Daigo whom he later turned against.
swap.clue: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.
